No changes made. Here's the assessment of `release/v1`:

## Green lights

- **Build:** `go build ./...` — clean
- **Vet:** `go vet ./...` — clean
- **Tests:** full `go test ./...` — all packages pass, no failures
- **Code hygiene:** no TODO/FIXME/HACK markers in non-test Go code
- **Rename completeness:** no lingering `intropy.dev` references in code, docs, or web
- **Branch state:** in sync with `origin/release/v1`
- **Tags:** `v1.0.0`–`v1.0.2` already exist, so the release line is flowing

## Uneven edges (non-blocking, your call)

1. **Untracked planning artifacts** — `docs/brainstorms/` (2 files) and `docs/plans/` (4 files) sit untracked in the worktree. `coverage.out` is properly ignored; these aren't. They should stay out of the release branch (the history even shows a commit `docs: remove plans and analysis docs from release branch`), so I'd suggest adding them to `.gitignore` in a small housekeeping commit — or just leaving them untracked.
2. **History quality** — the 42 commits ahead of `main` include a bare `Formatting` commit and nested merge sandwiches (`feat/dashboard-tracing` ↔ `release/v1` crossed twice). Not worth rewriting at this point, but worth noting for the release notes / changelog.
3. **Tag coverage** — `v1.0.2` is the latest tag; verify it points at the commit you intend to ship, since several fixes landed after the merge at HEAD (`c35c1991`). If the tag predates the domain-rename and message-wiring work, you'll want `v1.0.3` or an rc tag.

**Verdict:** functionally release ready. The only item I'd act on before merging to `main` is confirming where `v1.0.2` points relative to HEAD, and tidying the untracked docs. If you want, I can check the tag positions and prepare the merge to `main` via PR.

name: test

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      # Must precede `go build`: the web package embeds web/dist via go:embed,
      # so the SPA has to exist before the Go build reads it.
      - name: Build dashboard SPA
        run: npm ci && npm run build
        working-directory: web

      - name: Build
        run: go build -v ./...

      - name: Test
        run: go test -race -v ./...

      - name: Vet
        run: go vet ./...

      - name: Check formatting
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(gofmt -l .)" ]; then
            echo "The following files need formatting:"
            gofmt -l .
            exit 1
          fi

  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Build dashboard SPA
        run: npm ci && npm run build
        working-directory: web

      # The integration tests clone real repositories and run git commit,
      # which needs an identity. Dev machines have one from their global git
      # config; CI runners do not.
      - name: Set git identity
        run: |
          git config --global user.email "ci@intropy.io"
          git config --global user.name "CI"

      # The deploy tests drive the real kustomize binary. Without it those tests
      # skip, which would leave the render and diff logic — the part most likely
      # to break silently — untested.
      - name: Install kustomize
        run: |
          if ! command -v kustomize &> /dev/null; then
            curl -sSfL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/master/hack/install_kustomize.sh" \
              | bash -s -- 5.8.1 /usr/local/bin
          fi
          kustomize version

      - name: Build
        run: go build -v ./...

      - name: Test
        run: go test -race -v -tags integration ./...

content.text:
Ran every check from both workflows locally (read-only — the only new files are the SPA build output under `web/dist`, which is gitignored; your worktree still shows only the pre-existing untracked `docs/` folders).

## test workflow (the one that gates the PR)

| Check | Local result |
|---|---|
| Build dashboard SPA (`npm ci && npm run build`) | ✅ built in 731 ms |
| `go build -v ./...` | ✅ |
| `go test -race -v ./...` | ✅ all pass with race detector |
| `go vet ./...` | ✅ |
| `gofmt -l .` | ✅ empty — no unformatted files |

## integration job

| Check | Local result |
|---|---|
| `go test -race -v -tags integration ./...` | ✅ all pass (with kustomize present here, so the deploy/render/diff tests actually ran rather than skipped) |

## release workflow (tag push)

- `.goreleaser.yaml` and `.github/scripts/update-homebrew-formula.sh` both exist ✅
- The "Verify tag matches go.mod" step only echoes the tag — it can't fail. (Mild observation: the name overpromises; `go.mod` carries no version. Not a pass/fail risk.)
- The two things I can't simulate locally: `TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret availability and GHCR/cosign permissions. If a previous tag (`v1.0.2`) released successfully through this workflow, those are proven.

**Verdict:** the test workflow will pass on the PR — I reproduced every step of both jobs locally and everything is green. The only release-workflow risks are secrets/permissions, which look fine given prior tag releases succeeded. One caveat: the integration tests on CI runners lack a git identity and kustomize is installed fresh there — both are handled by the workflow's setup steps, and the tests passed locally with the same tooling in place.
